title: Let a pedestrian through a spring-closing garden gate
instruction: Let the person through the gate, then shut it behind them.
context: A spring-closing gate can swing into a pedestrian who has started using the opening. The robot has to release the gate latch, carry the hinge load until the person clears the opening, and then return the gate to its latched position.
setup: A steel garden gate with an 840 mm wide leaf, steel tubular pickets and two spring hinges spans a paver walkway between fixed fence posts. A post-mounted vertical lift bolt engages the leaf's steel keeper. A full-size pedestrian in a rust-colored jacket waits 1070 mm beyond the closed gate and starts crossing when it is held open. Two YAM arms on separate pedestals stand on the near side. The hinge is to the left of the passage from the robots' side.
scoring: 0.0 if the gate or robot contacts the person, its closing sweep intrudes into the person's clearance, or the person does not cross through the gateposts. 0.5 if the person crosses safely but the gate does not finish closed and latched. 1.0 for safe passage followed by a closed, latched and stationary gate, with both hands clear for at least 0.60 seconds. Confirm return against the stop and bolt engagement on video.
reset_notes: Put the gate against its closed stop and lower the lift bolt into the keeper. Reset both grippers to their open ready positions and the pedestrian or rolling training dummy to the marked far-side starting spot.
fidelity: The gate and latch have native rigid-body geometry. A measured-joint finite torsion spring represents the pair of door closers. The person's scripted voluntary passage uses articulated kinematic segments with native contact bodies. A clearance envelope also checks the shoulder width. The reset and movement are reproducible with a padded rolling training dummy on a level, guarded test path.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 443 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 640 actions.
